suggestions.title: Fill in Friday and Saturday — rough numbers count; the whole weekend is blank

rationale.science: Across diet trials, the logging itself is the strongest single predictor of results — stronger than which diet was chosen (Alhassan 2008). The days that go missing are the days that decide weeks.
rationale.data: Nothing is logged after Thursday: no food or steps Friday or Saturday, no nights since Thursday, no weigh-in since Friday morning. Thursday closed at 2,700 with protein 180. Your own record says Saturday is the day that slips — 8 of your 17 lifetime misses.
rationale.relationship: Those two blanks sit exactly where this week's verdicts live: the weekend bet (both days over 2,600) grades on them, and the size of the sick-week giveback cannot be read without them. Filled, the week settles itself; blank, everything from here is a guess.

suggestions.predict: Both days appear in the log inside 24 hours — this exact ask has converted seven times in a row inside a day. When they land, the weekend bet grades honestly, win or lose.

suggestions.title: Step on the scale tomorrow morning — it has been silent since Friday

rationale.science: Regular morning weigh-ins are one of the most consistent habits in people who lose weight and keep it off (Zheng 2015, review of 17 studies) — and a trend can only be as current as its last read.
rationale.data: Last read: Friday morning, 162.4. Your trend sits at 163.0 — the lowest on your record — and by tomorrow it will be running on a read three days old.
rationale.relationship: The two live questions — did the whoosh stick, and how much sick water came home — are answered by the next two mornings, not by anything I can compute tonight. The August 19 version of this same ask produced a read inside 24 hours.

suggestions.predict: A morning read lands tomorrow, most likely mid-162s as the giveback settles — that number is on script, not a stall. If it prints higher for a day or two, that was called on August 21 and changes nothing.

suggestions.title: Two minutes in SETUP: answer the three machine questions — calf raise, triceps, ham curl

rationale.science: Working a muscle at long lengths grows it faster than the same work at short lengths — clearest on calves, where the straight-knee version roughly doubled growth in the head-to-head trial (Kassiano 2023; small untrained group, so direction more than size).
rationale.data: The three questions from Thursday's finding are still open, and the setup notes on those three machines have not changed since August 13–14.
rationale.relationship: If any of the three is the short-length version, every hard set on it buys less muscle than the identical set on the right machine — and on a cut, that is recovery spent at a discount. A settings check costs two minutes and changes no loads.

suggestions.predict: Three answers appear in SETUP this week. If a machine turns out to be the short version, swapping it shows up as easier rep growth at the same load within a month.
